clue.text: Rock concert cleared by university in eg New Jersey, America

indicators.note: one group of letters sits inside another, as something placed in a pen

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of cow, so a new one is a young animal

indicators.note: a cleared-out word has had its contents emptied, leaving only its two outside letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of the word survive
standard abbreviation for university
A is a common abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A rock concert in New Jersey gets emptied out by the local college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock concert' reads as music, but 'Rock' alone is the definition. A Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, so a new one is its young.
explanation.definitionFit: Calc-tufa is a porous limestone deposited by calcareous springs, so it is a type of rock.

clue.text: Heartlessly commandeer Christian

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: to co-opt is to take over or appropriate for one's own use

explanation.walkthrough: CO-OPT has five letters, so its heart is the middle O; removing it leaves COPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Copt is a member of the ancient Egyptian Christian church, so an example of a Christian.

clue.text: Wretched poetic service led by Mark!

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
the Royal Navy is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A miserable church service in verse, introduced by someone called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name, but with the exclamation mark it is the command 'note this!', which is LO. 'Poetic' labels the answer as a literary word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorn is a literary word for forsaken and forlorn, which makes it a fair poetic equivalent of wretched.

clue.text: Best shackle sails and rigging?

parts.note: the top one is the best
to hamper is to restrict movement, like a shackle

explanation.surface: The finest restraints for holding a ship's sails and rigging in place.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a loose description rather than a dictionary phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Top hamper is the upper weight of a ship — its upper sails, spars and rigging — considered as encumbrance above deck.

clue.text: Firework dispute over "Fire Act" I violated

parts.note: a feud is a long-running quarrel

indicators.note: something violated has been broken and damaged, so its letters fall out of order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A row over a piece of fire legislation that has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts FEUD above the rest. The answer's display form keeps the French apostrophe, which the grid ignores.
explanation.definitionFit: Feu d'artifice is the French term, borrowed into English, for a firework or a fireworks display.

clue.text: Method of printing two picture cards within one capture

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so one group of letters goes into another

parts.note: to net something is to catch it
king and jack are court cards, also called picture cards

explanation.surface: A printing technique for reproducing a pair of illustrated playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture cards are the king, queen and jack; two of them sit inside the word for capture, with one in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkjet printing sprays tiny droplets of ink onto paper, a common technique for home printers.

clue.text: Palm trembling having lost skin when climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from the bottom upwards
losing the skin strips away the outermost layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: quaking means shaking with fear

explanation.surface: A hand shaking after a graze, as someone scrambles up a rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm' suggests a hand, but it is the tree. QUAKING loses Q and G, and UAKIN then reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nikau is a palm tree native to New Zealand, the most southerly growing palm species.

clue.text: Abandoned Juliet, upset, mean about brood

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards
about means surrounding, so one word goes around another

parts.note: to mean something is to denote it
a hen broods by sitting on eggs

explanation.surface: Juliet was jilted, distraught, while some cruel person sulked nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' and 'brood' look like a nasty person moping, but they are verbs, and 'upset' turns the whole container upward, not just the letter for Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, so jettisoned is a synonym of abandoned in the past tense.

clue.text: Colours in spray caused by wild brown otter

indicators.note: wild means untamed and out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild otter splashing through a river throws up a shimmering rainbow spray.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene of a splashing otter is all surface; 'brown otter' supplies exactly the ten letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent-bow is a rainbow formed in the mist above a waterfall or rushing stream.

clue.text: Circumnavigation including India is a bonus

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the rest

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'a' pound a day
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a plus is an added advantage

explanation.surface: A round-the-world voyage that takes in India counts as a perk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' here means 'each', which is PER; the phrase 'a bonus' holds I between its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A periplus is a voyage round a coast or sea, or an account of one, hence a circumnavigation.

clue.text: Dean for one again buys round after dropping an ecstasy

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to take a thing can mean to buy it, as in 'I'll take it'
E is slang for a tablet of ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone called Dean buys another round of drinks after losing a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buys round' reads as standing drinks, but RETAKES is turned round to SEKATER and one E dropped. Christopher Dean won Olympic ice-dancing gold with Jayne Torvill in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Dean is a famous British ice dancer, so he is an example of a skater.

clue.text: Chuck bagging nothing with reportedly quiet gun

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a bag, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to fling is to throw
O looks like zero
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so a word stands for one that sounds the same

parts.note: peace is quiet, and the word sounds the same as this spelling

explanation.surface: Throw away an empty bag, along with a gun said to be silent.
explanation.walkthrough: FLING takes in O and W to give FOWLING, then PIECE, which sounds like peace. 'Bagging' fits a shooting scene but here means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A fowling piece is a light shotgun designed for shooting wildfowl and birds, so it is a kind of gun.

clue.text: Like a carnivore like another? Self-contradiction number one

parts.note: a paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself
number one is a nursery euphemism for urinating

explanation.surface: A zoologist puzzles over an animal that resembles one predator which itself resembles another, calling it a self-contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' looks like a ranking, but it is the childish word for a wee. The definition's double 'like' is itself the paradox: an animal resembling a carnivore that resembles another.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradoxurine means belonging to or resembling the palm civets, genus Paradoxurus, which are carnivores related to the mongoose family.

clue.text: Blunt cocked-up rating that's nasty, burying British and Scotch

indicators.note: what is buried disappears from view, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: brusque means abrupt and blunt in manner
BR is an abbreviation for British

indicators.note: cocked up means tilted upward, so in a down entry the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: an able seaman, or AB, is a naval rating
ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A tactless, bungling sailor's foul remark, with talk of burying Britain and whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt cocked-up' reads as one phrase, but 'cocked-up' belongs to 'rating', the naval sense of an ordinary seaman. 'Burying' here means getting rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: Usquebaugh is the old Gaelic-derived name for whisky, literally water of life, so it means Scotch.

clue.text: Loquacious bishop sits on case involving another

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting on something means placed directly above it

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so one letter goes inside the word

parts.note: the ablative is a grammatical case in Latin
a second bishop, so another B

explanation.surface: A chatty bishop sitting in on a court case that implicates a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' sounds legal but is grammar. A second B goes inside ABLATIVE after its A, and the first B sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Babblative is a rare word for given to babbling, so it is a synonym for talkative or loquacious.

clue.text: Duck's upper surface mostly covered in down?

indicators.note: something covered is wrapped inside, so it goes within another word

parts.note: to down a drink is to sup it

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a cap is the top covering of something

explanation.surface: A duck's back is largely coated in soft feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like feathers, which fits a duck, but it is the verb meaning to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The scaup is a diving duck of northern waters, closely related to the tufted duck.

clue.text: Problem for grasses in trade union in favour of cutting back work

parts.note: TU is the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: to cut into something is to enter it, so one piece goes inside another
going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: toil is hard work
pro means for

explanation.surface: Union members who inform on colleagues back cuts to working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasses' suggests informers, British slang for people who tell on others, but the definition means cereal plants such as oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulip root is a disease of oats caused by eelworm, making the stem base swell like a bulb, so it afflicts cereal grasses.

clue.text: I see blackguard wearing contraceptive collar

indicators.note: something worn is inside clothing, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: the pill is the oral contraceptive
I plus C, which sounds like 'see'
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Someone spots a scoundrel who is on the pill, wearing a collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' is split as the letter I plus C, which sounds like see; both pairs go inside after the first letter of the contraceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccadill is a stiff ornamental lace collar worn around 1600, from which London's Piccadilly takes its name.

clue.text: Unlimited refund amended after knight boards taxi perhaps not called for in Germany

indicators.note: after places one section behind the other in reading order
to board a vehicle is to get inside it
without limits means the boundaries are gone, so first and last letters drop

parts.note: Uber is a ride-hailing taxi firm
N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the remaining letters change their order

parts.note: the word as written, before its ends go

explanation.surface: A full refund is given after a knight climbs into a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxi perhaps' needs a brand name rather than a synonym. 'Unlimited' means the refund word loses both ends before being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unberufen is German for unbidden or uncalled-for, used as an exclamation like touch wood to avert bad luck.

clue.text: Clubs once more prepare set of principles

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
to redo is to do or make ready again

explanation.surface: Sports clubs once again draft their mission statements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests golf or societies, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed or statement of beliefs, from the Latin for 'I believe', so a set of principles.

clue.text: Weird chap by Rachel, short-headed sort

indicators.note: weird means strange and out of the ordinary, so the letters end up in an odd order

parts.note: all twelve letters, including the little word in the middle

explanation.surface: An odd man next to Rachel, who is rather a curt type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word, but its letters are needed in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A brachycephal is a person with a broad, short skull, from Greek for short and head.

clue.text: Hot old sensational naked nymph

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap
O is an abbreviation for old
lurid means shockingly sensational

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a steamy, bare nymph from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: LURID stripped of L and D leaves URI.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is one of the beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise, and loosely any alluring young woman or nymph.

clue.text: Liberal breaking dilemma down

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering it, so one letter goes inside a word

parts.note: a fix is an awkward predicament
L for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician cracks under a hard choice and feels low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like dejection, but it is soft fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Flix is an old word for fur or the soft under-hair of animals such as beavers, which is down.

clue.text: Hollow dull sound after tons dumped under base of truck

indicators.note: in a down entry, under places a section below another
the base is the bottom, the last letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: dumped means thrown away, so that letter goes

parts.note: a thud is a heavy dull noise
T for tons

explanation.surface: A hollow thud as tons of cargo are tipped out from the back of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' seems to describe the sound, but it is the definition. THUD drops T and sits under K.
explanation.definitionFit: Khud is an Anglo-Indian word for a pit, ravine or deep valley, so a hollow in the land.

clue.text: Everywhere in half of 13, society is swinging both ways

indicators.note: to swing both ways is slang for bisexual, so one letter is swapped for that two-letter abbreviation
half of a word is its first five of ten letters

parts.note: the opening half of the answer to 13 down
S for society

explanation.surface: Everywhere you look in the whisky world, society is going both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: In USQUE the S for society becomes BI, the slang abbreviation for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubique is Latin for everywhere, best known as the motto of the Royal Artillery and Royal Engineers.

clue.text: Girl trouble — I see lengthy account

parts.note: Meg is a girl's name
ill as a noun is misfortune or trouble
ah is the noise of understanding

explanation.surface: Hearing a girl's tale of woe, the listener sighs: here comes a long story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' here is the exclamation, not I + C as at 17.
explanation.definitionFit: A megillah, from the Hebrew scroll read at Purim, is slang for a long, tediously detailed story.

clue.text: Increasingly breathing with difficulty internally, getting lift north of the border

indicators.note: only the inside is wanted, so the outermost letters are discarded

parts.note: wheezier is the comparative of wheezy

explanation.surface: Someone gasping more and more on a climb in the Scottish hills.
explanation.walkthrough: WHEEZIER loses its W and R. 'North of the border' means in Scotland, as seen from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Heezie is a Scots noun for a hoist or lift, from the Scots verb heeze, to raise.

clue.text: Bent down earth cable between ends of old fuse board

indicators.note: something between two things sits inside them, separating them
the ends of words are their final letters

parts.note: the final letter of each of the three words
E for earth, as on electrical wiring
a flex is a flexible electric cable

explanation.surface: An electrician's notes on wiring an earth cable into an old fuse board.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical scene is consistent, but 'fuse board' is just two words supplying final letters; the first end comes before the cable and the other two after.
explanation.definitionFit: Deflexed is a botanical term for bent or turned sharply downward, as of petals or leaves.
